Jaivantāyana, ‘descendant of Jīvanta,’ is mentioned in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad as a teacher, with śaunaka and raibhya, of rauhiṇāyana.
Foot notes iv. 5, 26 (Mādhyaṃdina). The name is recognised by Pāṇini, iv. 1, 103.

Jaivala or jaivali, ‘descendant of Jīvala,’ is the patronymic of Pravāhaṇa in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka and Chāndogya Upaniṣads. jaivali, the king, in the Jaiminīya upaniṣad brāhmaṇa is the same person.
Foot notes vi. 2, 1 (kāṇva = vi. 1, 1 Mādhyaṃdina), where the form is jaivala.
